title: A push anywhere starts the edition by itself: a cross-repository credential, or pages that load what they show
note: Dev, 27 October 2026, revised at the editor's word (no workflow runs on a timer). Today a push to the press builds the edition, and each repository takes it on its own next push. A push to data, team, site or updates cannot start the press's build: GitHub lets a workflow start runs only in its own repository unless it holds a credential for another. Two ways, not exclusive: (1) a GitHub App or a fine-grained token, installed on the six, used only to start the next workflow (Actions: write; or Contents: write if the editor prefers pushes across repositories), so data's push starts the edition and the edition's publish starts the four sites' deploys, within minutes; (2) the direction already under way: pages draw what they show from its owner when they open (articles, records, briefs already do), so a change to data or refs needs no site build and no site commit at all, and editions are needed only for a site's own frames. PROJECT-003 phase 2 also stops committing built editions to git. The editor decides (1).
